title: DATA MODELING
subtitle: Start from the queries the product runs, then choose keys and indexes that make each one cheap.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

items: Start from the queries the product actually runs, not from the nouns.
Choose keys and indexes that make each hot query a single index lookup or range scan.
Default to Postgres; deviate only with a reason (write volume → Cassandra, flexible docs → DynamoDB/Mongo, search → Elasticsearch).

blocks.text: Normalize by default (one place to update). Denormalize deliberately for a hot read path, and say how the copy stays in sync (CDC, async job).

items: List the two or three hottest queries first.
Make each one a key lookup or a single index range scan.
Default to Postgres; switch only with a reason you can state.
Normalize by default; denormalize deliberately for a hot read and say how the copy stays in sync.
Choose the partition key from the hottest query if you will shard.

blocks.text: "The hot query is a user's posts, newest first, so the posts table gets an index on (author_id, created_at DESC)."
